# Job Qualifications Reference

**Generated by `refresh_qualifications.py` — do not hand-edit.** Re-run the script
to pick up sheet changes.

Source: the "Qualification" tab of the Headless Headhunter sheet, pulled live.
<https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vRg7oze-BnheKtSvQH2ApktuRYyWaXOuvE9hgke4puccxX4Gs5I9-xAfxaKgRoYxYh6W1DlyqSA9e2c/pubhtml#gid=0>

These are the keywords/qualifications recruiters and hiring managers screen for,
per job title. **128 titles.**

> **Source caveat, from the sheet itself:** _"All Qualification are based on the United States Market, other countries Qualification for the same job title may differ"_

That caveat is load-bearing. Where the sheet carries a geography-specific row —
**Python Dev (India)**, **Full Stack - Canada**, **EU - Full stack**,
**EU - Front End**, **Cloud Engineer (Canada)**,
**Canada - Business Intelligence Analyst**, **Game Developer UK** — use that row
for that market instead of the US row. Do not union the variants; that dilutes
each list.

## How to use this

Pick the ONE job title you are applying to, take its list, and make sure those
tokens appear in your resume **bullets** as WHAT (the keyword) + HOW you used it
+ WHY (a plain business reason a layman understands) + WHERE (the job/project it
happened in). Target 75% of the list, with most of it in the first half of page
one. A token that appears only in a skills section has no WHERE and does not
count. See `resume_method.md` and `video_qualification_method.md` for the rules.

**Tier prefixes** — keep these straight, they signal priority:
`Rare:` / `Bonus:` / `Nice to Have:` / `Extra Credit:` mark **differentiators,
not requirements**. `Industry:` means domain knowledge to name explicitly.
Untiered lines are the **required set** that coverage is scored against.

**On wording:** every line is reproduced verbatim from the sheet, including its
typos and inconsistent punctuation — the literal token is what gets matched
against a resume and against a recruiter's boolean search, so correcting one
would silently break coverage. Titles with a typo in the source are marked
`[sic]`; body text is left exactly as written.
